title: EASM findings: the three drill-down levels and what the risk fields mean

prose.text: Findings are the risks EASM records against an organization's internet-facing assets. Their field list and types are in the contract; this subject holds what the fields mean and how to read deeper.

prose.label: Risk fields.
prose.text: {{risk-level}} {{severity-score}} {{exploit-likelihood}} The literal formats of these values are open {{gap:risk-value-formats}}.

drill-down.statement: A finding can be read at three depths: details, evidence (the subset of the asset's scan output attributable to the finding) and scan output (the complete scan output).

quotes: def get_finding_details(self, org_id: str, finding_id: str) -> APIResult[FindingDetails]:
This is a subset of the scan output obtained for the associated asset that can be attributed to the finding.
Retrieves the complete scan output for a finding based on the specified ID.

evidence-shape.statement: Evidence and scan output share one shape, `content` (the scan output text) and `source_type` (the scanning service, such as Web, Network, Certificate or DNS).

source_type.description: The scanning service used to detect the risk, such as Web, Network, Certificate, or DNS scans.
The scanning service used to detect the risk, such as Web, Network, Certificate, or DNS scans.

risk-level.statement: `risk_level` ranges over Low, Medium, High and Critical, and `risk_score` is a score from 1 to 100 that the contract types as a string.

expect.description: The risk level assigned to the finding ranging from Low, Medium, High, and Critical.
A risk score computed for the finding ranging from 1 to 100

severity-score.statement: `severity_score` is the CVSS score, 1 to 10, where applicable.

expect.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score that indicates the qualitative measure of severity of a vulnerability using a numerical value ranging from 1 to 10, if applicable.

exploit-likelihood.statement: `cisa_likelihood` indicates whether the vulnerability is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and `epss_likelihood` is the EPSS probability of exploitation in the wild; both are strings and apply where relevant.

expect.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) likelihood indicates the probability of a vulnerability being exploited in the wild, if applicable.

quotes: Indicates whether a vulnerability is listed in the <a href=\"https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog\"

scan-type.statement: `scan_type` names the scanning service that uncovered the risk, with Web, Network, Certificate and DNS scans given as examples.

expect.description: The scanning service that was used to uncover the risk, such as Web, Network, Certificate, and DNS scans.

category-type.statement: `category` classifies a finding (examples: Exposure, Vulnerability, Misconfiguration), `type` is a sub-classification within it, and `status` is the finding's workflow state from discovery to closure.

expect.description: The finding's classification such as Exposure, Vulnerability, or Misconfiguration.
Indicates the finding's current status in its workflow tracked from discovery to closure
The finding's type which is a sub-classification within the assigned category

stale.statement: `is_stale` marks an asset not detected in a scan for over 30 days.

expect.description: A Boolean value that indicates if the asset was not detected in a scan for over 30 days and is therefore marked as stale

country-profile.statement: `country` is the geographical location of the asset the finding is on, and `profile_id` is the ID of the Discovery Profile through which the finding was detected.

expect.description: The geographical location of the asset to which the finding is associated
ID of the Discovery Profile through which this finding was detected

description-osint.statement: A finding's `description` is gathered from open-source intelligence, such as the National Vulnerability Database, and Zscaler's research team.

quotes: A detailed description of the finding gathered from open-source intelligence, such as the National Vulnerability Database (NVD), and Zscaler's research team.

description-untrusted.statement: Through MCP, a finding's description arrives from tools not flagged as untrusted (`zeasm_list_findings`, `zeasm_get_finding_details`) even though its text comes from outside the tenant; treat it as untrusted text.
description-untrusted.conditions: Follows from description-osint and the MCP flagged set, which covers only the evidence and scan-output finding tools; the flag criterion is authorship by a party without tenant credentials.

scan-type-values.title: The complete set of scan_type values
scan-type-values.detail: The SDK model declares scan_type with no enumeration. The contract now describes it as the scanning service, such as Web, Network, Certificate and DNS scans, which gives examples rather than a closed list, and the literal strings returned are not shown.
scan-type-values.blocks: mapping every scan_type value to a scanning service

risk-value-formats.title: Value formats of the risk fields
risk-value-formats.detail: The contract now states risk_level ranges over Low, Medium, High and Critical, risk_score over 1 to 100, severity_score is CVSS 1 to 10, cisa_likelihood reflects KEV listing and epss_likelihood is the EPSS probability. Still open: the literal strings of cisa_likelihood (a flag or a label) and epss_likelihood (a 0 to 1 fraction or a percentage, since both are strings), the finding status values, and whether country is a name or a code.
risk-value-formats.blocks: filtering or ranking findings on CISA, EPSS, status or country values
